text: {"lessons":["Repeatedly selling only positions above my average cost shows how strongly I favor realizing gains and avoid realizing losses; I should base each sell decision on future prospects, not my purchase price or the pleasure and pain of locking in a result.","After selling winners, I bought more of every stock over several periods, then made no changes as the account fell. I should set portfolio-level risk and position limits, rebalance deliberately, and avoid automatic buying or inaction driven by recent losses.","With prices moving randomly, past price changes do not provide a reliable trading signal. I should focus on diversification and a consistent plan rather than trying to time the market from recent moves."]}
